subject: Transport retry policy: field ask + runtime exception workaround
messages:
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@chartwise.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Strange 503 bursts from your API during nightly sync

Hi Grace,

We started seeing intermittent 503s from the /v1/generate endpoint during our nightly batch ingest (02:30-03:00 PT) over the last three nights. The attached chartwise-error-log.txt contains timestamps and request ids — you'll see the spikes cluster at ~02:38. These failures cause our orchestration to mark a chunk as failed and re-run the whole job which doubles our downstream latency.

Quick ask: do you have a recommended client-side retry policy (retries, backoff, idempotency guidance) we should apply immediately? Longer-term we want to avoid duplicate processing on retries — is there any header or server-side idempotency option we can use today?

We can share more traces if helpful. We have an active POC and are trying to keep the demo green for next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Lee
Platform Lead, ChartWise
--
Attachment: chartwise-error-log.txt (text, 38 KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@chartwise.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange 503 bursts from your API during nightly sync

Tom — thanks for the log, that was helpful. We're sorry this is affecting the demo.

Immediate proposal (what ChartWise can apply in the next 24h):
- Client-side short-term: exponential backoff with jitter, max 5 attempts, base delay 250ms (250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 4s).
- Treat 429 and 503 as retryable. For 4xx (other than 429) do not retry.
- Include a unique request-id per logical operation in the client (X-ChartWise-Request-Id) so your side can dedupe work.

Short-to-medium-term ask for us (runtime):
- Can runtime treat a subset of 503s as transient and surface a Retry-After when queued?
- Is there an idempotency header we can support at the API layer (X-Redwood-Idempotency or similar) so retries do not create duplicate downstream effects?

Karthik / Logan / Marissa — copying you to triage. ChartWise needs a near-term workaround and a roadmap answer on idempotency so they can safely enable retries.

Tom — attaching a short mutual-action-plan (chartwise-mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with the immediate steps and owners; I can push the SDK patch to ship a recommended retry default this week if we have runtime guidance.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: chartwise-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 KB)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange 503 bursts from your API during nightly sync

Grace — quick read of the logs Tom attached shows a pattern where a small pool of inference workers reports transient queue pressure (spikes lasting 30–90s). The runtime currently returns plain 503 when a request is rejected for capacity; we do not consistently surface Retry-After.

Questions for runtime:
- Can we make 503 responses include Retry-After when the rejection is for queueing/capacity vs permanent errors? Even a coarse Retry-After (3s) would let clients back off quickly and avoid hammering.
- Would it be feasible to accept an idempotency header (X-Redwood-Idempotency) and route requests with the same token to an accept-once flow for stateless generation calls? I understand that's more complex for stateful flows but should be possible for single-shot generate calls.

Short-term SDK work: I can add a default retry policy to our JS and Python SDKs (configurable) and expose an opt-in idempotency header artifact so ChartWise can begin passing a token. But if runtime ignores it then it won't help.

Log excerpt (from chartwise-error-log.txt):
---
2028-04-09T02:38:12Z request_id=rw-9b2a status=503 reason="queue_full" worker=az1-gpu-12
2028-04-09T02:38:14Z request_id=rw-9b2b status=503 reason="queue_full" worker=az1-gpu-12
2028-04-09T02:38:45Z request_id=rw-9b7x status=200 latency=380ms worker=az1-gpu-14
---

If runtime can emit Retry-After and optionally accept an idempotency token, we can reduce retries that cascade into more pressure.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Sales Engineering
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-09T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Strange 503 bursts from your API during nightly sync

Thanks for the context. Short triage from Runtime: the 503s labeled "queue_full" are triggered by the serving runtime's admission controller when the continuous-batching queue exceeds configured thresholds. Root cause appears to be a short spike in concurrent windowed requests (likely a batched job overlap on ChartWise side).

Feasible immediate actions (this sprint):
- Server-side: Add a coarse Retry-After header for queue-based 503s. We can ship a conservative default of Retry-After: 3s. Low risk. (Jira: SRV-12345)
- SDK: Logan can add the exponential-backoff+jitter default this week. That combined with Retry-After will reduce hammering.

Feasible medium-term (3–8 weeks):
- API idempotency header: we can introduce an X-Redwood-Idempotency token for single-shot /generate calls and accept-once semantics when used against stateless models. Caveats: we need to document behavior across retries, cache TTL, and cross-instance coordination. Work estimate: 2–3 sprints to implement reliably and to add telemetry.
- Routing: optionally allow a field-level routing override so heavy nightly jobs can be routed to a dedicated pool (Dedicated capacity or a low-priority pool) if ChartWise wants to self-isolate. That's a product/ops conversation.

I'll create SRV-12345 and attach the quick patch for Retry-After; small risk and we can backfill tests. For the idempotency header we'll scope required changes and propose an API contract doc.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@chartwise.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-10T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transport retry policy: field ask + runtime exception workaround

Tom — short summary and next steps so you're unblocked for the demo: 

1) Immediate (tomorrow): ChartWise should enable exponential backoff with jitter in your client (we recommend max 5 attempts, base 250ms). Logan will push an SDK patch with this default by EOD tomorrow and publish config docs.
2) Very short-term (this sprint): Runtime will add Retry-After on queue-based 503s (SRV-12345). Karthik is pushing a conservative Retry-After: 3s patch; this should land in the canary infra next week.
3) Medium-term (3–8 weeks): We will scope and provide an API contract for X-Redwood-Idempotency for single-shot generate calls. This will be opt-in initially and documented with cache TTLs and semantics.

If ChartWise wants the simplest path to avoid duplicate downstream work in the meantime, we recommend you generate a per-logical-operation token (X-ChartWise-Request-Id) and use client-side dedupe. Once our idempotency header ships you can switch to that header.

I'll update the mutual action plan (attached) with owners and dates. Can you confirm you want the SDK default enabled for your POC? If so I'll mark the HubSpot deal CHW-0923 as "SDK retry opt-in" and drive the patch.

Thanks again for the quick signal — we'll keep you posted as SRV-12345 progresses.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Sr Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
